title: AccountMenu
wrapsNative: MonarchIconButton with MonarchAvatar as its content, MonarchMenu with MonarchMenuItem, MonarchRadio and MonarchDivider, MonarchThemeToggle; or MonarchBottomSheet on phones
summary: A recipe, not a component: the signed-in person's menu, an avatar button that opens a menu (or a sheet on phones) with who is signed in, Profile and Settings, a workspace switcher, the color scheme and Sign out.
whenToUse: At the end of the top app bar, or at the foot of a navigation rail or drawer, as the one place for the person's account, workspace and appearance.
whenNotToUse: For a screen of account settings, use a settings screen with MonarchSwitchRows and sections. For switching workspaces as the main task of a screen, use a list of workspaces.
api: IconButton(onClick = { open = true }, modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Account menu for …" }) { MonarchAvatar(image = …, name = …, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Sm, decorative = true) }

DropdownMenu(expanded = open, onDismissRequest = { open = false }) { …; DropdownMenuItem(text = { Text("Profile") }, onClick = …); …; MonarchThemeToggle(scheme = scheme, onSchemeChange = { scheme = it }, size = MonarchThemeToggleSize.Sm); DropdownMenuItem(text = { Text("Sign out") }, onClick = …, colors = MenuDefaults.itemColors(textColor = MonarchTheme.colors.dangerStrong)) }
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }) { …; MonarchThemeToggle(scheme = scheme, onSchemeChange = { scheme = it }); MonarchButton("Sign out", …, variant = MonarchButtonVariant.Danger) }

states.name: closed
states.description: The avatar, with a presence dot when given a status, as the icon button that opens the menu.

states.name: open (menu)
states.description: A Material 3 menu: the name and email, Profile and Settings, the workspaces as radio items with the current one checked, the theme toggle, and Sign out in the strong danger color.

states.name: open (sheet)
states.description: On phones, the same choices in a modal bottom sheet with full-width buttons and the segmented theme toggle, which leaves room at the largest font scale.

appearance: The trigger is MonarchAvatar in its initials or picture colors inside a 48dp icon button. The menu is the Material 3 menu on the raised background role with Monarch's medium radius; the header uses the strong body and muted caption text roles; Sign out uses the strong danger role. The sheet uses the Material 3 sheet surface. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AccountMenu as one component with user, workspaces, theme and callback props, and renderLink for router links. On Android it is a recipe, as on iOS: a MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu already give the trigger, focus, keyboard and TalkBack behavior, so no Monarch type is added. The theme choice is MonarchThemeToggle bound to the app's MonarchScheme; apply it with MonarchTheme(scheme = …) at the root and persist it with MonarchThemeToggleStorage. The web's "sheet on phones" option is the second example: a MonarchBottomSheet, where a dropdown menu at the largest font scale would scroll. The web's workspaceSlot and items props are the app's own menu items; navigation is the app's (onClick). Monarch bundles no icons, so the menu items carry no glyphs unless the app adds leadingIcon.
accessibility: The icon button is named "Account menu for <name>"; the avatar inside is decorative so the name is read once.
The header's name and email are one element.
Workspace items carry the radio button role and the selected state, so the current workspace is announced, not only shown by the radio mark.
"Switch workspace" is a heading, so TalkBack users can jump to it.
MonarchThemeToggle reads its options and the selected scheme; Sign out is a word, not only a color.
Material 3 gives each menu item a row at least 48dp high; the icon button is 48dp.
edgeCases: With one workspace, leave the switcher out.
A long name or email wraps in the header; at the largest font scale prefer the sheet.
Keep the scheme with rememberSaveable or the app's settings store so it survives a restart, through MonarchThemeToggleStorage.
